title: Polar alignment reports error in raw arcseconds ("1800.0 arcseconds", "Up 2287.9\""), which no one adjusting a wedge can read

Every readout named in the summary is wired: _measurement_panel.dart:371/405/441/466 (az/alt/total tiles + the threshold caption), _right_panel.dart:245/253/261, _completion_panel.dart:57/58/59 (both headline branches) and :154/163/169/212/221/227 (all six Before/After numbers), _history_panel.dart:152/176/292, all_sky_target_reticle.dart:178/269. Grepping the whole polar_alignment tree for toStringAsFixed leaves only the RA/Dec sexagesimal helpers in _measurement_panel and the improvement-percent in _history_panel, and the only surviving raw-arcsecond text is the fixed 30/60/120 ring labels in _error_visualization.dart, which the summary explicitly scopes out. evidence: Severed the production call site by rewriting the completion headline back to '${totalError.toStringAsFixed(1)} arcseconds' / '${...}" off'. test/screens/polar_alignment/polar_alignment_wizard_ux_test.dart went red on both 'a run that reached its target reads in arcminutes' and 'a run that missed its target reads in arcminutes too'; restored and it is green again. Worth recording: the shipped unit test polar_alignment_error_format_test.dart is logic-only and does NOT catch that severance — only the two widget tests, which assert the rendered strings, do.

title: The History button in the polar alignment header appears to do nothing — the panel it opens is off-screen below the config column
repairSummary: Added a `_applyingExternalIndex` re-entrancy guard to _CompactTabLayoutState in packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/polar_alignment/polar_alignment_body_layout.dart: _syncTabController sets it around the `_tabController.index = index` assignment (try/finally) and _onTabChanged returns early while it is set, so pushing the provider's index INTO the controller during build can no longer bounce straight back into the provider. Added packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/polar_alignment/polar_alignment_compact_history_test.dart, which drives the wizard at 430x932 (below the 700 compactBreakpoint), taps the Errors tab, taps History, and asserts tester.takeException() is null AND that 'Alignment History' is built and inside the viewport. With the guard line removed the test goes red with 'Tried to modify a provider while the widget tree was building'; with it restored it is green. dart format clean.
reasoning: The claimed mechanism is all present and correct on the wide layout: the screen owns _configScrollController (polar_alignment_screen.dart), hands it to the configuration column's SingleChildScrollView (_configuration_panel.dart:22), and a ref.listen on polarAlignmentUiStateProvider.select(showHistoryPanel) fires on the false->true edge, calls setCompactTabIndex(0) (verified index 0 == the 'Settings' tab in _CompactTabLayout) and animates to maxScrollExtent in a mounted/hasClients-guarded post-frame callback; the History button carries a Tooltip. But the compact path — the one the fix had to add setCompactTabIndex for, and the only one where the button was previously 100% dead rather than merely below the fold — was never exercised: every shipped test pumps at 1400x900. Driving it at 430x932 shows the fix works AND throws. Chain: the listener writes compactTabIndex, _CompactTabLayoutState.build calls _syncTabController(0), which assigns TabController.index; TabController._changeIndex with no duration decrements _indexIsChangingCount BEFORE notifyListeners, so the existing `indexIsChanging` guard in _onTabChanged does not fire and _onTabChanged writes setCompactTabIndex from inside build. Riverpod asserts. This is newly introduced, not pre-existing: before the fix nothing outside this widget ever moved the tab, so `_tabController.index != index` always short-circuited and the assignment never happened. It is a debug/profile-mode assertion (release builds elide it), but the write-back mid-build is unsound in any mode, and the phone layout is a shipping path (apps/mobile consumes the shared router). Residual nit I am not counting: because the reveal targets maxScrollExtent, a long history list scrolls to its last row rather than to the 'Alignment History' header — the panel is on screen either way.
evidence: Probe at 430x932 with the shipped code: 'Tried to modify a provider while the widget tree was building' at PolarAlignmentUiStateNotifier.setCompactTabIndex <- _CompactTabLayoutState._onTabChanged <- ChangeNotifier.notifyListeners <- TabController._changeIndex <- TabController.index= (stack captured in full). Severing ONLY the setCompactTabIndex(0) line makes the same probe fail differently — 'Found 0 widgets with text "Alignment History"' — proving both that the tab-set is what makes the button work on a phone and that it is what triggers the exception. Severing the whole listener body makes the shipped wide-layout test 'History scrolls its panel into view' fail with 'panel at Rect.fromLTRB(51.0, 645.0, 259.3, 663.0), viewport height 560.0', i.e. the original below-the-fold defect. After the repair the probe reports the panel at Rect.fromLTRB(51.0, 510.0, 259.3, 528.0) in a 932-high viewport with no exception.

title: Polar alignment config controls stay visually enabled during a run but silently ignore clicks
reasoning: I checked the premise before the fix: every control in _configuration_panel.dart passes `isRunning ? null : ...`, so the clicks were already genuinely refused and the complaint really was the missing signal. The fix adds _buildSettingsLockedNote ('Settings are locked while aligning — press Stop to change them.') above the groups when isRunning, and wraps Essential/Common/Advanced in _dimWhileRunning -> Opacity(SkotiqTokens.opacityMuted). The claim that this stays above the disabled threshold checks out numerically: opacityMuted is 0.6 and opacityDisabled is 0.38 (packages/skotiq_ui/lib/src/theme/skotiq_tokens.dart:381/384). This is disclosure, but it is not the DISCLOSURE-ONLY failure shape: the behaviour was already correct and the finding was specifically that nothing said so. Residual, not a defect: the ExpansionTile headers keep an un-gated onExpansionChanged, so Common/Advanced still fold and unfold while dimmed — consistent with the stated goal of letting the operator still READ the hemisphere/binning the run is using.
evidence: Severed by deleting the `if (isRunning) ...[_buildSettingsLockedNote(colors), SizedBox(height: 12)]` block. 'the configuration column says why it is locked mid-run' went red while the paired negative test 'an idle wizard does not claim its settings are locked' stayed green, so the assertion discriminates in both directions. Restored, green.

title: Re-opening Polar Alignment shows the previous run's "Alignment Complete" screen instead of a fresh start
reasoning: dispose() calls _releaseFinishedRun(), which returns unless the snapshotted phase is complete or error, then posts a frame callback calling controller.reset() inside try / on PolarAlignmentBusyException. I checked the ways this shape usually fails: (1) the phase enum has exactly five values (idle, measuring, adjusting, complete, error — packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/polar_alignment_config.dart:20) so complete+error IS the complete terminal set; there is no third terminal phase left standing. (2) PolarAlignmentController.reset() is a synchronous void and PolarAlignmentStateNotifier.reset() throws PolarAlignmentBusyException synchronously, so the try/catch genuinely catches rather than wrapping an un-awaited Future. (3) PolarAlignmentScreen has exactly one mounting site, app_router.dart:360, so it is not embedded in a tab whose switch would dispose it and silently discard a result the operator still wanted. (4) _controller/_phase are snapshotted in build because `ref` is invalid inside a ConsumerState dispose, which is the right way round. A run still in flight is deliberately untouched.
evidence: Severed by replacing _releaseFinishedRun() in dispose() with a comment. 'leaving a finished run reopens the wizard on idle' went red (the phase stayed complete after the pop); restored, green. One window I am not claiming as covered because a widget test cannot reach it: if the operator pops while the history row is still being written, the busy exception is swallowed and the terminal screen survives one more entry. The fixer documents that deliberately and it is better than forcing a reset over an in-flight save.

title: Flat wizard Frame Count can only be changed one click at a time — 27 clicks to go from the default 30 to 3
reasoning: The typeable field is real and complete: _FrameCountInput in packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/flat_wizard/flat_wizard_screen/tuning_controls.dart is now stateful, with FilteringTextInputFormatter.digitsOnly + LengthLimitingTextInputFormatter(3), onSubmitted -> _commit, a focus listener -> _commit, an explicit onTapOutside that drops focus on EVERY platform (Flutter's default _EditableTextTapOutsideAction deliberately does not unfocus a touch on Android/iOS, so without it the focus-loss commit never fires on the shipping mobile path), a 1..999 mirror of FlatWizardNotifier.setFrameCount's clamp, normalise-after-clamp in _commit so the field can never disagree with the run, didUpdateWidget that refuses to overwrite mid-typing, and steppers that keep the field in sync and disable at the ceiling. I checked the multi-surface trap: all three tabs — Quick Capture, Multi-Filter Batch and Sky Flats — use this same _FrameCountInput (capture_mode_controls.dart:54, :118, :203), so there is no unfixed second copy. Ordering also works out for the worst case the fix exists to prevent: TapRegion fires onTapOutside on pointer DOWN while a button's onPressed fires on pointer UP, so typing 3 and reaching straight for Start Capture commits the 3 before the run reads it. NOTE for the record: the onTapOutside handler is itself a repair made by the earlier (context-exhausted) verify pass on this shard, not by the original fixer — I re-verified it rather than assuming it.
evidence: Severed by deleting the onTapOutside handler: 'a typed frame count commits when the field loses focus' went red; restored, green. The three originally-shipped tests all end with tester.testTextInput.receiveAction(TextInputAction.done) and never exercise focus loss at all, so that assertion is the only thing standing between the field and the type-then-tap-Start defect.
